listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Saturday, November 14. Here is what matters today. Our lead story is the nationwide ground stop that disrupted air travel across the United States. US officials say the disruption was caused by old equipment overloading. They say it was not a cyber-attack. The BBC has an explainer on what is known and what to do if you are affected. Now the front page. The White House says President Trump, Russian President Putin and Chinese President Xi plan a joint meeting in China next week. It describes the talks as unprecedented. A spokeswoman says Trump will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons. In basketball, Alperen Sengun scored 43 points and pulled down 12 rebounds. The Houston Rockets beat Utah 125 to 118 in NBA Cup play. It was the Jazz's eleventh straight loss. In politics, Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins won the race for governor of Alaska. He replaces a Republican. At 37, he will be the youngest governor in the state's history. In architecture technology, a company called qentin uses AI to make scanned buildings searchable. Facility managers can ask questions in natural language to find assets and check safety features. Now the sections. In tech, Alibaba released an open code review tool that pairs fixed pipelines with an AI agent. Hacker News is also discussing an allegation that Nvidia created GPU scarcity by funding startups to buy its chips. In politics, The Lever reports on allegations of corruption behind a large data center project in New Mexico. Some Republican state officials are also appealing to revive mail-in voting limits for the 2028 election. In world news, President Trump says the status quo is what Gulf Arab allies want as the Iran war reaches a stalemate. In New Orleans, all passengers were rescued after a cruise ship collision, and thirty-two people are in hospital with non-critical injuries. In sports, the 49ers list Trent Williams and Dre Greenlaw as questionable for Sunday's game against the Cowboys. Receiver Mike Evans is out. In UFC news, eight people received six-month prison sentences in Abu Dhabi over the hotel brawl involving Merab Dvalishvili. In Atlanta, a condo high-rise of up to 225 feet is proposed in Old Fourth Ward. A street overhaul is also set to break ground in Little Five Points. In architecture, McNeel is rolling out Rhino 9 and bringing AI into the product. Archiboost raised 6.2 million dollars for its AI platform. In science, a National Geographic documentary follows researchers finding new life in the Southern Ocean. Astronomers also used the Chandra observatory to explain repeated outbursts from a giant unstable star. That is the brief. Have a good day.

lead.title: What we know about the ground stop and what to do if you're affected
lead.note: A nationwide ground stop disrupted air travel across the United States. US officials say the disruption was caused by old equipment overloading and not a cyber-attack. The BBC explainer sets out what is known about the ground stop and what to do if you are affected. The stated cause matters because an equipment failure and a cyber-attack raise different questions about security and about how much the aviation system relies on aging technology. For anyone who travels, or who depends on schedules tied to flights, a halt like this is easy to feel and hard to plan around. This is the official explanation so far, and the summary does not say how the equipment failed or how long the disruption lasted.
